outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by outlining the factual circumstances that led to the litigation, the parties involved, and the procedural trajectory from the original complaint to the appellate decision. It explains how the case arose on the Cameo platform, the content of the videos, and the rationale for the district court’s dismissal before the appeal.
subtopics: Facts of the Cameo transaction and Kimmel’s use of the videos
Parties: George Santos, Jimmy Kimmel, ABC, Disney
District Court’s Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal and grounds (fair use & state‑law preemption)
Appellate review standards: de novo and permissible supplemental evidence

outline.chapter_title: 2. Copyright Infringement and the Fair‑Use Defense
outline.description: This chapter dissects the copyright claim and the court’s application of the statutory fair‑use test. It explains each factor, how the "purpose and character" of the use is analyzed, and how the court treats bad‑faith allegations. The doctrinal anchors—case law on transformation, the role of subjective intent, and the "coffee‑house” criterion—are all tied to the facts of this case.
subtopics: Statutory framework: U.S.C. § 107 and the four fair‑use factors
Analysis of purpose/character: transformative use principles and prior cases (Andy Warhol, TCA Television)
Nature of the work, amount used, and market impact factors as applied to the videos
Bad‑faith and “good‑faith” considerations: Harper & Row, Swatch, Authors Guild
Conclusion that fair use bars infringement at pleading stage

outline.chapter_title: 3. State‑Law Claims: Breach and Fraudulent Inducement
outline.description: This chapter tackles the secondary claims. It distinguishes claim types, examines the contractual basis for the breach of contract and implied‑contract allegations, and explores how Illinois and New York law treat third‑party benefits and implied contracts. It also explains the failure of the fraudulent‑inducement claim, focusing on the requirement to allege out‑of‑pocket loss.
subtopics: Breach of contract under Cameo Terms of Service: presumption against third‑party enforcement, Illinois contract law
Implied‑contract claim: New York’s "meeting of minds" test and required essential terms
Preemption discussion and why the court declined to rule on it
Fraudulent inducement: New York’s loss requirement and plaintiffs’ failure to allege it

outline.description: The final chapter brings together the equitable evaluation of the facts, the statutory framework, and the procedural decision. It shows how the appellate court follows the rules of civil procedure, applies the equitable doctrine of fair use, and dismisses the state‑law claims, culminating in the affirmed judgment.
subtopics: De novo review and permissible judicial notice of copyright registrations
Logical flow from facts to fair‑use determination
Reaffirmation of district court’s dismissal and conclusion of appeal
